finding: There is no live range for this job yet, so this is a first build, and it stays held. Built totals, labor only (no parts), stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Nissan Sentra, midsize 2016 Nissan Rogue, truck 2017 Nissan Titan and luxury 2015 Infiniti Q50 each about $60-$80 (0.5 hr). How this compares: that sits at the top of the two priced benchmarks, RepairPal's $49-$72 and the Kelley Blue Book average of $60-$72 quoted second-hand, so the build is slightly high for a paid rotation. Candidly, this is a menu-price service and the menu price often sits below a book-time build: many shops charge a flat fee, fold the rotation into an oil change, or do it free. Rotation is commonly free for the life of the tires where the tires were bought (Discount Tire, Costco, Les Schwab, Firestone, Sam's Club and others), so $0 is a normal price and a driver should check that first. One maker's own maintenance-plan reference booklet (Mopar) says its dealer payment for a tire rotation is capped at $10, which shows how little the service is valued inside a plan. A shown range of about $0-$80 would be honest. How solid the labor times are: weak, and the same single figure everywhere. No maker-printed time for a plain maintenance 'rotate tires' operation was found for any vehicle. The 0.5 hr low end is the Nissan and Infiniti all-models warranty time for swapping all four wheels and resetting the tire pressure system during a pull diagnosis, the nearest stated operation and a little more than a bare rotation; it is not class-specific, so the truck is not shown as costing more even though heavier wheels plausibly take longer. The 0.5 hr high end is a tire chain's general 'about 30 minutes', not a book time. The Tesla service-manual figures used before (0.29, 0.36, 0.66) have been taken out of the range because the manual prints them with no unit; they remain as labelled cross-checks only. What is still missing: a manufacturer document that prints a time for 'tire rotation'. Checked without success on this pass: GM tire warranty bulletins 00-03-10-003 and 20-NA-159 (tire replacement operations only, rotation mentioned as advice), Honda bulletin 20-081 (mount and balance and alignment only), Volkswagen circular VWP-18-05 (gives an operation number for oil change with tire rotation but no time), FCA, Ford, Hyundai, Subaru, Mazda and Toyota tire or pull bulletins (no rotation line), and maker prepaid-maintenance documents (no times). Also not found: a posted paid rotation price from a chain. Cars with different tire sizes front and rear, or directional tires, cannot be rotated the usual way.
extras: A quote may add: wheel balancing (often sold with the rotation as 'rotate and balance'); a tire pressure sensor reset or relearn; including a full-size spare in the pattern; removing and refitting wheel locks or hubcaps; extra labor for dual rear wheels, oversized or heavy off-road tires; remounting tires on the wheels where sizes differ front to rear or tires are directional (a larger job); a brake inspection or a wheel alignment recommended from the tire wear found; shop supplies and sales tax. Before paying, check whether the rotation is free where the tires were bought or included with an oil change or a maintenance plan.
held_reason: no manufacturer-stated labor time for a plain 'rotate tires' operation was found; every class rests on one Nissan/Infiniti 0.5 hr tyre-swap pull-diagnosis operation and a tire chain's 'about 30 minutes'. Tesla figures (no unit printed) are now cross-checks only
